requirements.heading: Standards Tree
requirements.text: Registrations in the standards tree MUST be either:

requirements.heading: Standards Tree
requirements.text: The registration proposal MUST be published as an RFC.

requirements.heading: Standards Tree
requirements.text: The format MUST be described by a formal standards specification produced by the submitting standards- related organization.

requirements.heading: Standards Tree
requirements.text: Media types in the standards tree MUST NOT have faceted names, unless they are grandfathered in using the process described in Appendix A.

requirements.heading: Vendor Tree
requirements.text: When a third party registers a type on behalf of someone else, both entities SHOULD be noted in the Change Controller field in the registration.

requirements.heading: Unregistered x. Tree
requirements.text: Also note that if a generally useful and widely deployed type incorrectly ends up with an "x-" name prefix, it MAY be registered using its current name in an alternative tree by following the procedure defined in Appendix A.

requirements.heading: Functionality Requirement
requirements.text: Media types MUST function as actual media formats.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: All registered media types MUST be assigned top-level type and subtype names.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: Type and subtype names MUST conform to the following ABNF:

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: For this reason, <type-name> and <subtype-name> SHOULD be limited to 64 characters.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: The choice of top-level type MUST take into account the nature of media type involved.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: New subtypes of top-level types MUST conform to the restrictions of the top-level type, if any.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: Additionally, various protocols, including but not limited to HTTP and MIME, MAY impose additional restrictions on the media types they can transport.

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: If a "charset" parameter is defined for a particular subtype of text, it MUST be used to specify a charset name defined in accordance to the procedures laid out in [RFC2978].

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: As specified in [RFC6657], a "charset" parameter SHOULD NOT be specified when charset information is transported inside the payload (e.g., as in "text/xml").

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: If a "charset" parameter is specified, it SHOULD be a required parameter, eliminating the options of specifying a default value.

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: If there is a strong reason for the parameter to be optional despite this advice, each subtype MAY specify its own default value, or alternatively, it MAY specify that there is no default value.

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: Finally, the "UTF-8" charset [RFC3629] SHOULD be selected as the default.

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: Regardless of what approach is chosen, all new text/* registrations MUST clearly specify how the charset is determined; relying on the US-ASCII default defined in Section 4.1.2 of [RFC2046] is no longer

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: If explanatory text is needed, this SHOULD be placed in the additional information section of the registration.

requirements.heading: Text Media Types
requirements.text: Plain text MAY allow the stacking of several characters in the same position in the text.

requirements.heading: Multipart and Message Media Types
requirements.text: All subtypes of multipart and message MUST conform to the syntax rules and other requirements specified in [RFC2046] and amended by Section 3.5 of [RFC6532].

requirements.heading: Additional Top-Level Types
requirements.text: Definition of a new top-level type name MUST be done via a Standards Track RFC; no other mechanism can be used to define additional type names.

requirements.heading: Structured Syntax Name Suffixes
requirements.text: Media types that make use of a named structured syntax SHOULD use the appropriate registered "+suffix" for that structured syntax when they are registered.

requirements.heading: Structured Syntax Name Suffixes
requirements.text: By the same token, media types MUST NOT be given names incorporating suffixes for structured syntaxes they do not actually employ.

requirements.heading: Structured Syntax Name Suffixes
requirements.text: "+suffix" constructs for as-yet unregistered structured syntaxes SHOULD NOT be used, given the possibility of conflicts with future suffix definitions.

requirements.heading: Deprecated Aliases
requirements.text: In such cases, a preferred name MUST be chosen for the media type, and applications MUST use this to be compliant with the type's registration.

requirements.heading: Deprecated Aliases
requirements.text: However, a list of deprecated aliases by which the type is known MAY be supplied as additional information in order to assist applications in processing the media type properly.

requirements.heading: Parameter Requirements
requirements.text: Media types MAY elect to use one or more media type parameters, or some parameters may be automatically made available to the media type by virtue of being a subtype of a content type that defines a set of parameters applicable to any of its subtypes.

requirements.heading: Parameter Requirements
requirements.text: In either case, the names, values, and meanings of any parameters MUST be fully specified when a media type is registered in the standards tree, and SHOULD be specified as completely as possible when media types are registered in the vendor or personal trees.

requirements.heading: Parameter Requirements
requirements.text: Therefore, registrations MUST specify parameter value syntax.

requirements.heading: Parameter Requirements
requirements.text: New parameters SHOULD NOT be defined as a way to introduce new functionality in types registered in the standards tree, although new parameters MAY be added to convey additional information that does

requirements.heading: Canonicalization and Format Requirements
requirements.text: All registered media types MUST employ a single, canonical data format, regardless of registration tree.

requirements.heading: Canonicalization and Format Requirements
requirements.text: A permanent and readily available public specification of the format for the media type MUST exist for all types registered in the standards tree.

requirements.heading: Canonicalization and Format Requirements
requirements.text: This specification MUST provide sufficient detail so that interoperability between independent implementations using the media type is possible.

requirements.heading: Canonicalization and Format Requirements
requirements.text: This specification MUST at a minimum be referenced by, if it is not actually included in, the media type registration proposal itself.

requirements.heading: Interchange Recommendations
requirements.text: Universal interoperability of media types is not required, but known interoperability issues SHOULD be identified whenever possible.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: An analysis of security issues MUST be done for all types registered in the standards tree.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: However, regardless of what security analysis has or has not been done, all descriptions of security issues MUST be as accurate as possible regardless of registration tree.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: In particular, the security considerations MUST NOT state that there are "no security issues associated with this type".

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: Security considerations for types in the vendor or personal tree MAY say that "the security issues associated with this type have not been assessed".

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: Nevertheless, all known security risks MUST be identified in the registration of a media type, again regardless of registration tree.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: The security considerations section of all registrations is subject to continuing evaluation and modification, and in particular MAY be extended by use of the "comments on media types" mechanism described in Section 5.4 below.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: o Any security analysis MUST state whether or not they employ such "active content"; if they do, they MUST state what steps have been taken, or MUST be taken by applications of the media type, to protect users of the media type from harm.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: All media types SHOULD state whether or not they employ compression; if they do, they SHOULD discuss what steps need to be taken to avoid such attacks.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: Types SHOULD always document whether or not they need such services in their security considerations.

requirements.heading: Usage and Implementation Non-Requirements
requirements.text: explicitly intended for limited use, this MUST be noted in its registration.

requirements.heading: Publication Requirements
requirements.text: Media types registered in the standards tree by the IETF itself MUST be published as RFCs.

requirements.heading: Publication Requirements
requirements.text: As stated previously, standards-tree registrations for media types defined in documents produced by other standards-related organizations MUST be described by a formal standards specification produced by that organization.

requirements.heading: Publication Requirements
requirements.text: Additionally, any copyright on the registration template MUST allow the IANA to copy it into the IANA registry.

requirements.heading: Fragment Identifier Requirements
requirements.text: In particular, media types that use a named structured syntax with a registered "+suffix" MUST follow whatever fragment identifier rules are given in the structured syntax suffix registration.

requirements.heading: Additional Information
requirements.text: Various sorts of optional information SHOULD be included in the specification of a media type if it is available:

requirements.heading: Additional Information
requirements.text: In the case of a registration in the standards tree, this additional information MAY be provided in the formal specification of the media type format.

requirements.heading: Preliminary Community Review
requirements.text: Notice of a potential media type registration in the standards tree SHOULD be sent to the media-types@iana.org mailing list for review.

requirements.heading: Preliminary Community Review
requirements.text: Registrations in other trees MAY be sent to the list for review as well; doing so is entirely OPTIONAL, but is strongly encouraged.

requirements.heading: Submit Request to IANA
requirements.text: Media types registered in the standards tree by the IETF itself MUST be reviewed and approved by the IESG as part of the normal standards process.

requirements.heading: Provisional Registrations
requirements.text: A provisional registration MAY be submitted to IANA for standards- tree types.

requirements.heading: Provisional Registrations
requirements.text: Provisional registrations MAY be updated or abandoned at any time.

requirements.heading: Review and Approval
requirements.text: Recognition from the IESG MUST be obtained before a standards-tree registration can proceed.
